mainTopic: Trusting a כותי or a transgressor on שחיטה and מצוות: supervision, the eating test, accepted versus written מצוות, and רבא's checked-knife rule
overview: This amud deals with when we may trust meat slaughtered by someone who is not fully careful about מצוות. It opens at the end of a ברייתא about a כותי's שחיטה. אביי and רבא read opposite halves of that ברייתא and disagree about a Jew who only goes out and comes in while the כותי slaughters. The גמרא then questions the ברייתא's test of having the כותי eat one bird's head. It asks how one head can prove all the birds are kosher, and whether the כותים even believe birds need שחיטה. The answer is that once the כותים accepted a מצוה, they keep it carefully. This leads to a ברייתא with three opinions about a כותי's מצה. The גמרא concludes that the תנא קמא trusts the כותים only on written מצוות, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also trusts them on unwritten מצוות they accepted. Finally, the גמרא explains רבא's rule that a Jew who eats נבילות out of appetite may slaughter with a knife we checked, and it begins a supporting ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The string of birds: the כותי must eat one head
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the case of many birds a כותי slaughtered: cut off one bird's head and give it to him. If he eats it, his שחיטה may be eaten. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a string of birds, he cuts off the head of one of them and gives it to the כותי. If the כותי ate it, it is permitted to eat what he slaughtered. If not, it is forbidden to eat what he slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last line of a ברייתא about meat slaughtered by a כותי. When the Jew wasn't there, we test the כותי by seeing whether he himself will eat from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a כותי will not eat meat he knows was slaughtered improperly. So his willingness to eat shows the שחיטה was done right. For a group of birds, testing one is enough for all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: A string or bunch (of birds tied together)
Cuts off
Ritual slaughter
A Samaritan, the person whose שחיטה is being discussed

phrases.english: A string of birds,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא about a כותי's slaughter. Here the Jew came only after the birds were already slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: קוֹטֵעַ רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ.
phrases.english: he cuts off the head of one of them and gives it to him.
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כותי who did the slaughtering.

phrases.english: If he ate it, it is permitted to eat from his slaughtering,
and if not, it is forbidden to eat from his slaughtering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the Jew was not present for a כותי's שחיטה of birds, the כותי must eat the head of one bird. If he does, the birds are permitted; if not, they are forbidden.

steps.title: אביי and רבא each learn from a different half of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that אביי draws his proof from the רישא and רבא draws his from the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי makes a careful inference from the first part of the ברייתא, and רבא makes a careful inference from the last part.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that each אמורא will now read the same ברייתא from a different end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never mentions the in-between case of a Jew who goes out and comes in. So each אמורא figures out that case from what the ברייתא leaves unsaid. They read opposite halves and reach opposite results.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a careful inference from the exact wording
The first clause of a ברייתא or משנה
The last clause of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Abaye infers from the first clause,
Rava infers from the latter clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי דָּיֵיק מֵרֵישָׁא, רָבָא דָּיֵיק מִסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted as the source for the dispute between אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both אמוראים base their positions on the same ברייתא, each reading a different clause.

steps.title: אביי's inference: only standing over him works
steps.stepSummary: From the רישא, אביי infers that the meat is permitted only because the Jew stood over the כותי. Going out and coming in is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי infers from the first clause: the reason it is permitted is that the Jew is standing over him. But if the Jew goes out and comes in, it is not permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי points to the רישא, which permits the meat when a Jew stands over the כותי. He reads this as saying that anything less, such as going out and coming in, does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא chose the case of 'standing over him.' אביי reads that choice as a requirement, not just one example. So a Jew who keeps leaving and coming back has not supervised enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is (only) this, which hints that without it the rule would change
Standing right over him, watching the whole time
Going out and coming in, so only watching on and off

phrases.english: Abaye infers from the first clause:
The reason is that the Jew is standing over him,
but if he goes out and comes in, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי דָּיֵיק מֵרֵישָׁא: טַעְמָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out אביי's half of the announcement in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that יוצא ונכנס is not enough supervision for a כותי's שחיטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the ברייתא, which permits the meat specifically when the Jew stands over the כותי.

steps.title: רבא's inference: going out and coming in is fine
steps.stepSummary: From the סיפא, רבא infers that the eating test is needed only when the Jew arrived after the slaughter. Going out and coming in is good enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא infers from the latter clause: the reason a test is needed is that the Jew came and found that the כותי had already slaughtered. But if the Jew goes out and comes in, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points to the סיפא, which requires the test only when the Jew came and found the animal already slaughtered. He reads this as saying that going out and coming in needs no test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the סיפא's case, 'he came and found,' as the only case needing a test. A Jew who goes out and comes in is not in that case. So the meat is permitted without any test.

keyTerms.meaning: He came and found him, meaning the Jew arrived only after the שחיטה
It is perfectly fine

steps.confusionAlert: Both אמוראים are reading the very same ברייתא. Neither one is quoting a new source. They simply start from opposite ends, so the unmentioned middle case comes out opposite for each.

phrases.english: Rava infers from the latter clause,
the reason is that he came and found that he had slaughtered,
but if he goes out and comes in, it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא דָּיֵיק מִסֵּיפָא, טַעְמָא דְּבָא וּמְצָאוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite inference to אביי's in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that יוצא ונכנס is enough supervision for a כותי's שחיטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא, which requires the eating test only when the Jew came and found the animal already slaughtered.

steps.title: Challenge to אביי from the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: the סיפא seems to support רבא, so how does אביי deal with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אביי, the latter clause is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבא's proof into a question on אביי. The סיפא implies that only 'came and found' needs a test, so going out and coming in should be fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי relied on the רישא, but the ברייתא has two halves. Whoever argues from one half must also explain the other half. The סיפא, read like רבא reads it, contradicts אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a challenge
And according to (someone's view)

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, the latter clause is difficult,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's reading of the סיפא from step 4 to challenge אביי from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that יוצא ונכנס is not enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא limits the test to 'came and found,' which implies that a Jew who goes out and comes in needs no test.

steps.title: אביי: going out and coming in counts as 'came and found'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא includes going out and coming in within 'came and found,' so it too needs the test.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: going out and coming in is also called 'he came and found him.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by saying the case of going out and coming in falls under the סיפא's case. So the סיפא never implied that going out and coming in is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, every time the Jew comes back in, he is 'coming and finding' what happened while he was gone. So the סיפא's test covers that case too. This keeps his reading of the רישא intact.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
Calls it, meaning the ברייתא labels it this way

phrases.english: He could say to you:
going out and coming in also
is called 'he came and found him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: יוֹצֵא וְנִכְנָס נָמֵי ״בָּא וּמְצָאוֹ״ קָרֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to אביי in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining which case a term in the ברייתא covers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'came and found' means only a Jew who arrived after the שחיטה was over.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Came and found' also includes a Jew who goes out and comes in, so the סיפא agrees with אביי.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from the רישא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: the רישא seems to support אביי, so how does רבא deal with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, the first clause is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא does the mirror move. It uses אביי's proof from the רישא as a question on רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא permits the meat when the Jew is 'standing over him.' That implies that going out and coming in is not enough, which goes against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause is difficult, so there is a challenge from it

phrases.english: And according to Rava, the first clause is difficult,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 5, this time challenging רבא with אביי's reading of the רישא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that יוצא ונכנס is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא permits the meat because the Jew stood over the כותי, which implies that only full supervision works.

steps.title: רבא: going out and coming in counts as standing over him
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that going out and coming in is treated like standing over him, so the רישא already includes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: going out and coming in is also considered like standing over him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by putting going out and coming in inside the רישא's case. So the רישא never excluded it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, a Jew who keeps coming back in is supervising well enough to count as 'standing over him.' So both halves of the ברייתא fit his view. In the end, the ברייתא can be read either way, and the dispute between אביי and רבא stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Is considered like, is treated the same as

steps.whatToRemember: אביי and רבא argue about a Jew who goes out and comes in while a כותי slaughters. אביי treats it like 'came and found,' so a test is needed. רבא treats it like 'standing over him,' so the meat is permitted without a test. Each one explains the other half of the ברייתא by fitting this middle case into the half that matches his view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. When a source mentions only two cases, the argument is often about which side an unmentioned middle case belongs to.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
going out and coming in also
is considered like standing over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: יוֹצֵא וְנִכְנָס נָמֵי כְּעוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבא in step 7, mirroring אביי's answer in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining which case a term in the ברייתא covers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'standing over him' means only a Jew who watches the whole time without leaving.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Standing over him' also includes a Jew who goes out and comes in, so the רישא agrees with רבא.

steps.title: The ברייתא's case of a string of birds
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a Jew who finds a כותי holding birds cuts off a head and gives it to him to eat as a test.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way, if he found a string of birds in his hand, he cuts off the head of one and gives it to him to eat, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's case of birds, the line we saw in step 1, so it can examine it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the ברייתא taught that we test a כותי by having him eat from what he slaughtered. Here it applies the same idea to a bunch of birds. The Jew cuts off one bird's head and hands it to the כותי. If he eats it, we trust his slaughter of all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly; the same kind of case
A string or bunch of birds tied together
Birds
He cuts off its head

phrases.english: Similarly,
if he found in his hand a string of birds,
he cuts off its head, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." means the rest of the ברייתא: he gives the head to the כותי to eat. If he eats it, the birds are allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ, מָצָא בְּיָדוֹ דְּקוּרְיָא שֶׁל צִפֳּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the אביי–רבא debate back to the ברייתא's clause about birds, first seen in step 1, in order to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew who finds a כותי with a string of birds cuts off one head and gives it to him to eat. If he eats it, the birds are permitted.

steps.title: Maybe only that one bird was slaughtered properly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the test works. Maybe the כותי slaughtered only that one bird properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let us worry that maybe this one is the bird he slaughtered properly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's test. It asks how one eaten head can prove that all the birds are kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כותי knows which bird the head came from, he might eat it only because that one bird was slaughtered properly. The rest could be נבלות. Then his eating proves nothing about the other birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let us be concerned; we should worry
Perhaps; maybe
Properly; well

phrases.english: Why?
Let us worry that maybe this is the one
that he slaughtered properly!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? לֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא הַאי הוּא דַּהֲוָה שָׁחֵיט שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the test just quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that eating one bird's head proves all the birds were slaughtered properly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The test only works if the כותי cannot tell which bird the head came from. If he can tell, his eating proves only that one bird was slaughtered properly.

steps.title: The Jew hides the birds under his garment
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשה answers that the Jew hides the birds under the corners of his garment, so the כותי does not know which bird the head came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשה said (a memory aid: inserts, scalpel, into rams): the case is where he puts them under the corners of his garment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשה answers the challenge. The Jew cuts the head off while the birds are hidden, so the כותי cannot know which bird it came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the כותי knows which bird he is eating from. If the birds are hidden under the Jew's garment, the כותי cannot match the head to a bird. So if he eats it, he must believe that every bird was slaughtered properly.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists a sage's statements in order
He brings them in; he hides them
The corners of his garment

phrases.english: Rav Menashe said:
(A memory aid: inserts, scalpel, into rams)
phrases.notes: This is a memory aid listing three statements of רב מנשה in this מסכת: this one and two that come later. Some versions have it and some don't.

phrases.english: Where he puts them under the corners of his garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשֶּׁה: בְּמַכְנִיסָן תַּחַת כְּנָפָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא is talking about a situation where the birds are hidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כותי can see which bird the head came from, so the test proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The birds are hidden under the Jew's garment, so the כותי cannot tell which bird he is eating from.

steps.title: Maybe the כותי marked the good bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the כותי put a mark on the kosher bird's head, so he can recognize it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe he had put a mark in it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב מנשה's answer. Even with the birds hidden, the כותי might still recognize the head through a mark he made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiding the birds only helps if the head itself has nothing special about it. If the כותי secretly marked the one bird he slaughtered properly, he would recognize the head and eat it with no worry. The test would again prove nothing about the other birds.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or identifying mark
He placed; he gave
In it; inside it

phrases.english: And maybe a mark he had
put in it?
phrases.notes: He means a secret sign on the properly slaughtered bird, so the כותי would know its head.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא סִימָנָא הֲוָה יָהֵיב לֵיהּ בְּגַוֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב מנשה's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מנשה's answer that hiding the birds keeps the כותי from knowing which head he is eating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mark on the head would let the כותי recognize the good bird even without seeing where the head came from.

steps.title: The Jew crushes the head
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers that the Jew crushes the head, so any mark on it is destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: the case is where he crushes it thoroughly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers the worry about a mark. The Jew mashes the head before giving it, so nothing about it can be recognized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the head is crushed, any secret sign on it is gone. The כותי cannot tell which bird it came from. So if he eats it, that shows he trusts all the birds.

keyTerms.meaning: He crushes; he mashes
Thoroughly crushed; a strong crushing

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
Where he crushes it thoroughly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: דִּמְמַסְמֵס לֵיהּ מַסְמוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case further: the head is crushed so nothing about it can be recognized.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A secret mark could let the כותי recognize the good bird's head.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Jew crushes the head, so any mark is destroyed and the test works.

steps.title: Maybe the כותים think birds need no שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a deeper problem: maybe the כותים hold that birds do not need שחיטה according to the Torah, so his eating proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And maybe the כותים hold that there is no שחיטה for a bird from the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the whole test from a new angle. Steps 15 and 16 answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the worry was about which bird the כותי ate from. Now the worry is about what the כותי believes. If the כותים think birds need no שחיטה at all, a כותי would happily eat an unslaughtered bird, so his eating tells us nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold; they are of the opinion
Samaritans; a group who keep some parts of the Torah
Kosher slaughter
From the Torah itself

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same kind of question as the last two. Those asked whether the כותי knew which bird he ate. This one asks whether the eating test can work at all, given what the כותים believe about birds.
steps.whyThisMatters: The eating test only works if the כותי himself believes that what he eats must be properly slaughtered. If he does not, the whole test falls apart.

phrases.english: And maybe the Samaritans hold:
there is no slaughter for a bird from the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא קָסָבְרִי כּוּתִים: אֵין שְׁחִיטָה לָעוֹף מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the problem of recognizing the bird is solved, this attacks the test itself on a deeper level.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basic idea of the ברייתא's test: that a כותי eating the bird's head shows the birds were slaughtered properly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the כותים believe birds need no שחיטה from the Torah, the כותי would eat even an unslaughtered bird. Then his eating proves nothing.

steps.title: The details of שחיטה are not written either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on step 14. The five things that make a שחיטה invalid are also not written in the Torah, yet we still rely on the כותים for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic: pausing during the cut, pressing the knife, hiding the knife, cutting outside the right spot, and tearing out the pipes. Are any of these written in the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry from step 14 with a counter-question. Your worry would also apply to things we already accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said a כותי might not do שחיטה on birds, because the Torah never writes that birds need it. The גמרא replies that שהייה, דרסה, חלדה, הגרמה and עיקור also come from tradition and are not in the written Torah. Yet nobody doubts that we can rely on the כותים for these, so 'not written' cannot be the deciding factor.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning. It turns the other side's logic back on itself.
Pausing in the middle of the שחיטה
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth
Hiding the knife under the skin or the pipes while cutting
Cutting outside the proper area of the neck
Tearing the סימנים out of place instead of cutting them

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
interrupting, pressing, concealing,
phrases.notes: These are the classic things that make a שחיטה invalid. They are learned by tradition, not from a פסוק.

phrases.english: diverting, and ripping out:
are they written in the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the worry in step 14 by showing that it proves too much.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that a כותי cannot be trusted on a מצוה that is not written in the Torah
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same logic would stop us from trusting them on the five invalidations of שחיטה, which we clearly do trust them on.

steps.title: Once they took on a מצוה, they keep it fully
steps.stepSummary: The rule is that once the כותים accepted a מצוה, they keep it properly. The same is true for שחיטת עוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since they took these rules upon themselves, they took them on. Here too, since they took on שחיטה, they took it on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the principle that solves the problem. Whatever the כותים have accepted, they keep carefully, so we can trust them on birds too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is not whether the מצוה is written in the Torah. What matters is whether the כותים accepted it. Since they accepted the rules of שחיטה, the test with the bird's head from steps 9 to 13 works after all.

keyTerms.meaning: They took hold of it, meaning they accepted and keep this practice
Here too. It applies the same principle to the current case.

steps.whatToRemember: A כותי is trusted on any מצוה the כותים have accepted, even one that is not written in the Torah.

phrases.english: Rather, since they took hold of them,
they took hold of them.
phrases.notes: In other words, once they accepted these rules, they keep them carefully, so we rely on them.

phrases.english: Here too: since they took hold of it,
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא means שחיטה for birds.

phrases.english: they took hold of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the counter-question of step 15 into a positive rule that answers step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Establishes a general principle: what was accepted counts, not what is written
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כותי is only trusted on מצוות written in the Torah, so his eating of a bird proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כותי is trusted on any מצוה the כותים have accepted, so the test with the bird works.

steps.title: Trusting them on unwritten מצוות is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this exact question is debated by תנאים. The first opinion in a ברייתא says a כותי's מצה is permitted and even fulfills the מצוה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether they are trusted on things not written in the Torah is a dispute among תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: a כותי's מצה is permitted, and a person fulfills his obligation with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that the principle from step 16 is not agreed on by everyone. It starts quoting a ברייתא that shows the two sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא lets a person eat a כותי's מצה and even use it for the מצוה. Which תנאים actually argue about unwritten מצוות is worked out later. In step 26 the גמרא concludes that the argument is between the תנא קמא, who does not trust them on unwritten מצוות, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who does.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
מצה baked by a כותי
His obligation, meaning he fulfills the מצוה with it

phrases.english: And whether they are presumed reliable or not presumed reliable
in what is not written in the Torah is a dispute of תנאים,
as it is taught: the matza of a Samaritan is permitted,
and a person fulfills with it
his obligation on Passover.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַחְזוּק וְלָא אַחְזוּק בִּדְלָא כְּתִיבָא, תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the principle of step 16 inside a known מחלוקת of תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question of trusting כותים on unwritten מצוות is a dispute among תנאים. The ברייתא opens with the תנא קמא, who permits a כותי's מצה and lets one fulfill the מצוה with it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר forbids a כותי's מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees and forbids the כותי's מצה, because the כותים are not experts in the fine details of מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר forbids it, because they are not experts in the fine details of מצוות like Jews are.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the ברייתא. רבי אלעזר does not trust the כותים on details that are not clearly written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that even when the כותים keep a מצוה, they may not know its exact details. So he does not rely on their מצה. Step 22 will explain that the detail he has in mind is guarding the מצה (שימור).

keyTerms.meaning: Experts, people who know the rules well
The fine details of מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא permits a כותי's מצה, even for the מצוה. רבי אלעזר forbids it, because he holds the כותים are not experts in the details of מצוות (step 22 explains he means שימור).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying the כותים don't keep מצה at all. He is saying they may not know its exact details well enough to be trusted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar prohibits it,
because they are not experts
in the details of מצוות like Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by giving the opposing opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כותי's מצה is forbidden, because the כותים are not experts in the details of מצוות.

steps.title: A third opinion: כותים are extra careful with מצוות they accepted
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that any מצוה the כותים have taken on, they keep even more carefully than Jews do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: any מצוה that the כותים have taken on, they are much more careful with it than Jews are.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its third and last opinion about the מצה of a כותי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the כותים can be trusted, and even more than Jews, for מצוות they have accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר just said that כותים are not experts in the fine details. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers that for a מצוה they have accepted, they are actually more careful than Jews. So a כותי's מצה can be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: A group living in ארץ ישראל whose Jewish status and מצוה-keeping were in doubt.
They took hold of it, meaning they accepted that מצוה and keep it.
They are careful and exact.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Any מצוה that the Kutim have taken hold of,
they are much more careful with it than Jews are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion in the ברייתא, disagreeing with רבי אלעזר in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מצוות the כותים have accepted, they are more careful than Jews, so they can be relied on.

steps.title: Why say a permitted מצה also counts for the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the first opinion in the ברייתא and asks: if the מצה is permitted, isn't it obvious that it counts for the מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the מצה of a כותי is permitted, and a person fulfills his obligation with it on פסח. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back over the ברייתא line by line, starting with the תנא קמא. It asks why he needed to add that you fulfill the מצוה with this מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כותי's מצה is permitted to eat on פסח, it seems obvious that it can also be used for the מצוה. The second half of the line looks unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what extra lesson it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! The גמרא asks why something needed to be said at all.
He fulfills his obligation.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from step 17.

phrases.english: The matza of a Kuti is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation with it on Pesach.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts going back through the ברייתא, beginning with the תנא קמא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra words in the תנא קמא's statement: 'and a person fulfills his obligation with it'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מצה is permitted, it obviously works for the מצוה, so the extra words seem to add nothing.

steps.title: The extra words teach that כותים know how to guard מצה
steps.stepSummary: You might have thought the כותים don't know how to guard the מצה for the מצוה, so the ברייתא tells us they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that they are not experts in guarding the מצה, so the ברייתא teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The extra words teach that the כותים know how to do שימור properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצה can be fine to eat, because it is not חמץ, and still not count for the מצוה if it was not guarded for the מצוה. Without the extra words we might have allowed eating it but not using it for the מצוה. The ברייתא tells us it works for the מצוה too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. It introduces a mistaken idea that the statement comes to correct.
Guarding the מצה from becoming חמץ, with the מצוה in mind.
Experts, skilled.
It teaches us. It introduces the real lesson.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Permitted' and 'fulfills the מצוה' are two separate levels. 'Permitted' only means the מצה is not חמץ. Using it for the מצוה also needs שימור.

phrases.english: You might have said:
they are not experts in guarding the matza,
so it teaches us that they are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' question from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a new detail that the extra words teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כותי's מצה can be eaten but not used for the מצוה, because the כותים may not know how to do שימור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כותים do know how to guard מצה, so a person fulfills the מצוה with it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's worry is about guarding the מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר forbids the כותי's מצה because they don't know the fine details. The גמרא explains that he means שימור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר forbids it, because they are not experts in the fine details of מצוות. He holds that they are not experts in guarding the מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's line from the ברייתא again. It explains which 'fine detail' he has in mind: guarding the מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Fine details of מצוות' is a general phrase, and the גמרא pins it down to שימור. So רבי אלעזר and the תנא קמא disagree about one exact point: whether the כותים know how to guard מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The fine details of מצוות.
He holds, meaning this is his reasoning.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar forbids it,
because they are not experts in the fine details of מצוות.
He holds that they are not experts in guarding the matza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second opinion in the ברייתא and explains it using the idea of שימור from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר forbids the כותי's מצה because he holds they do not know how to guard it properly.

steps.title: Isn't רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל again and asks whether he is just repeating the תנא קמא, who also permits the מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: any מצוה the כותים have taken on, they are much more careful with it than Jews. But isn't that the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the third opinion in the ברייתא. It points out that it seems to match the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trust the כותים with their מצה. If they reach the same result, it is unclear why they are listed as two separate opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as.
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Any מצוה that the Kutim have taken hold of,
they are much more careful with it than Jews are.
Isn't that the same as the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the third opinion in the ברייתא and compares it with the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion is really separate from the תנא קמא's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions trust the כותי's מצה, so the third opinion seems to add nothing.

steps.title: They differ about a written מצוה the כותים never accepted
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא trusts the כותים with any מצוה written in the Torah. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts them only if they actually took that מצוה on.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a מצוה that is written in the Torah but that the כותים did not take on. The תנא קמא holds that since it is written, we trust them even though they did not take it on. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that if they took it on, yes, and if they did not take it on, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions differ in one case: a מצוה written in the Torah that the כותים never accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the fact that a מצוה is written in the Torah is enough to trust the כותים. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, what matters is whether they actually accepted it. A מצוה being written in the Torah is not enough for him.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them. It shows the practical case where two opinions differ.
That is written in the Torah.
Even though.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two different reasons for trusting the כותים: one is the written Torah, the other is what they actually took on and keep.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
in a מצוה that is written but that they did not take hold of.
The first tanna holds:
since it is written,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אַחְזִיקוּ בַּהּ,
phrases.english: even though they did not take hold of it, we trust them.
And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
if they took hold of it, yes, we trust them;
if they did not take hold of it, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23 by finding a case where the two opinions differ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a practical difference between the two opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about a written מצוה the כותים did not take on. The תנא קמא trusts them, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not.

steps.title: Then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל should have said 'if they took it on'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant to limit when we trust the כותים, he should have said 'if they took it on,' not 'any מצוה they took on.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of saying 'any מצוה that the כותים took on,' he should have said 'if they took it on'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 24 from the exact words רבן שמעון בן גמליאל used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'any מצוה they took on' sound like they widen the rule, as if even מצוות that are not written can be trusted. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wanted to narrow the תנא קמא's rule, the natural wording would be 'only if they took it on.' So his wording does not fit the explanation in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It introduces a problem with the explanation just given.
He should have said.

phrases.english: If so,
instead of 'any מצוה that the Kutim took hold of,'
he should have said 'if they took hold of it'!
phrases.notes: 'If they took hold of it' would sound like a limit on the תנא קמא's rule, and that is the meaning step 24 gave him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 24 using the wording of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 24 that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל narrows the תנא קמא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase 'any מצוה they took on' sounds like it widens the rule. A statement that narrows the rule would say 'if they took it on.'

steps.title: The real difference: an unwritten מצוה the כותים took on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation of the dispute. The two opinions differ about a מצוה not written in the Torah that the כותים took on anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they disagree about a מצוה that is not written in the Torah but that the כותים took on. The תנא קמא says: since it is not written, we do not trust them even though they took it on. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: once they took it on, they took it on, and we trust them.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 25 knocked down the earlier way of explaining the dispute, so the גמרא now offers a new one. The two opinions differ about a מצוה the Torah does not write, which the כותים took on anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא trusts the כותים only with מצוות written in the Torah. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds more: any מצוה they took on, even an unwritten one, is trusted. This explains his wording 'any מצוה they took on.' He is adding to the trust, not limiting it.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them (the practical case where the two opinions disagree)
That is not written (in the Torah)
They took it on, they held onto it as their practice
Once they took it on, they took it on, so they can be trusted with it

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: we trust the כותים only with מצוות written in the Torah. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: we also trust them with any מצוה they took on, even an unwritten one.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 24. There, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was explained as trusting the כותים LESS than the תנא קמא. Now he trusts them MORE, because he also includes unwritten מצוות they took on.

phrases.english: Rather, there is a difference between them
about a מצוה that is not written, and they took it on.
The first תנא holds:
since it is not written,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאַחְזִיקוּ בַּהּ – נָמֵי לָא;
phrases.english: even though they took it on, we still do not trust them;
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds:
once they took it on, they took it on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording objection of step 25 by giving a new explanation of the dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits trust to written מצוות the כותים took on, but that does not fit his wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: He widens trust to include unwritten מצוות they took on, while the תנא קמא trusts them only with written מצוות.

steps.title: רבא's rule: check the knife, then the transgressor may slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבא's statement. If a Jew eats נבילות only because he likes them, we may check a knife, give it to him, and eat what he slaughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main topic. רבא said: a Jewish transgressor who eats נבילות because he wants to, we check a knife and give it to him, and we may eat from his slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section. It goes back to a statement of רבא quoted earlier so it can explain it fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This transgressor sins only for convenience or taste, not to rebel against the Torah. So we may rely on his slaughtering, as long as we first make sure the knife is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: going back to a statement quoted earlier to discuss it fully
A Jew who regularly breaks a מצוה
Animals that died without kosher slaughter
For his appetite: he sins because he wants to, not out of rebellion
Checks the knife to make sure the blade is smooth, with no nicks

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for when we may eat from a slaughterer who does not keep the מצוות.

phrases.english: Now the matter itself. רבא said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבא's statement that was quoted earlier, on 3a.

phrases.english: A Jewish transgressor
who eats נבילות to satisfy his appetite
one checks a knife and gives it to him,
and it is permitted to eat from what he slaughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, going back to רבא's statement quoted earlier in the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew who eats נבילות out of appetite may slaughter with a knife we checked, and we may eat his שחיטה.

steps.title: Why we trust him: he won't pick forbidden over permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבא's reason. When kosher and non-kosher are equally available, this transgressor would choose the kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since he can do it the permitted way or the forbidden way, he would not leave the permitted and eat the forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's rule and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person sins only for convenience. When kosher slaughter costs him nothing extra, he has no reason to choose the forbidden way. So we assume he slaughtered properly.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The permitted and the forbidden
He would not leave or give up

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since there is a permitted way and a forbidden way,
he would not leave the permitted
and eat the forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא הֶתֵּירָא וְאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבא's rule from step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why may we rely on this transgressor's slaughtering?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With both options equally easy, he would not choose the forbidden one.

steps.title: Then why check the knife at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason. If he always chooses the permitted, his slaughtering should be allowed even without checking the knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even when the knife was not checked, it should also be permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason it just gave. If he never prefers the forbidden, why do we need to check the knife?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason 'he won't choose forbidden over permitted' seems to make him trustworthy in every case. That would make רבא's requirement to check the knife unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
When he did not check (the knife)

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כִּי לָא בְּדַק נָמֵי,
phrases.english: If so, even when the knife was not checked, it should also be permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כִּי לָא בְּדַק נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 28, because it seems to make checking the knife unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement in רבא's rule to check the knife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he would never prefer the forbidden, he should be trusted with any knife, so checking it should not be needed.

steps.title: He won't bother to get a better knife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: he would not go to the trouble of finding a new knife if his knife has a nick.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would not trouble himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. He picks kosher only when it is no extra effort, and replacing a bad knife takes effort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His good behavior only goes as far as convenience. If his knife has a nick, he would not bother to find a smooth one, so he would slaughter with the bad knife. That is why we must check the knife and hand it to him ourselves.

keyTerms.meaning: He would not go to any trouble

steps.whatToRemember: We trust a לתיאבון transgressor only when doing it the kosher way costs him no effort. That is why we check the knife for him.

phrases.english: He would not go to the trouble.
phrases.notes: He means: if the knife has a nick, he won't bother to look for a better one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29 by limiting the reason to cases with no extra effort.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He always chooses the permitted, so checking the knife is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: He chooses the permitted only when it costs no effort. He would not bother to replace a flawed knife, so we must check it.

steps.title: The רבנן offer רבא a supporting ברייתא about transgressors' חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן tell רבא that a ברייתא supports his view, and they begin quoting it: a case about the חמץ of transgressors after פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבא: A ברייתא was taught that supports you: The חמץ of transgressors, after פסח...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for רבא's rule. The רבנן start quoting a ברייתא about transgressors' חמץ after פסח, and its ruling comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has only explained רבא's rule with logic. Now it looks for an outside source. The ברייתא talks about people who sin with חמץ, so it may show how חכמים judge the behavior of a transgressor. We must wait for the rest of the ברייתא to see how it proves רבא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: That supports you. It introduces a source brought to back up someone's opinion.
Their חמץ (leavened bread)
Transgressors, people who sin
After פסח

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rava:
A baraita is taught that supports you:
The leavened bread of transgressors
phrases.notes: These are people who did not get rid of their חמץ before פסח.

phrases.english: after Passover

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logic of רבא's rule was defended in step 30, the רבנן now bring a ברייתא to support it.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that a Jew who eats נבילות out of appetite can be trusted to slaughter once his knife is checked, because he would choose the permitted when it is equally available.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the חמץ of transgressors after פסח. Only its opening appears here, and the ruling comes next.
